node.title: Endpoint norm-defect and complementary-factor identities
node.statement: For a hypothetical failure at the first strict A=3 endpoint, let H be the squarefree supported-slope form, R=product_(x in D)Q(x) the parameter norm, and O the aggregate omitted-domain-root count. There are forms J,S with J R=H^rho S, deg J=O<=m-1, and deg S=1+O<=m. If P_sat is the product of the at least 15m saturated domain points, there are complementary biforms Vbar,W with Q Vbar+P_sat W=H, deg_param Vbar=3m+1, deg_X Vbar<deg P_sat, and deg_X W<=rho-1. At least 2m+2 supported slopes are generic-rank, D-split, and parameter-transverse. The D x Z evaluation matrix is a full-row/full-column Reed-Solomon product-code word with exact column and row MDS excesses O and 1+O. These identities are necessary normal forms, not exclusions of the endpoint configuration.
